# Draft:Auto Queens (Documentary film)

Auto Queens is a 2025 Indian short documentary film directed by Sraiyanti and produced by Storiculture. The film [https://www.thehindu.com/entertainment/movies/meet-the-auto-queens-this-tamil-documentary-highlights-chennais-women-auto-drivers/article70401740.ece follows] women auto-rickshaw drivers in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, focusing on members of Veera Pengal Munnetra Sangam (VPMS), the first trade union for women auto drivers in the state. Through everyday moments of labour, organising, and family life, the documentary examines [https://thefederal.com/category/entertainment/auto-queens-chennai-women-auto-drivers-sraiyanti-haricharan-documentary-vpms-union-218780 gender], [https://www.thenewsminute.com/flix/auto-queens-portrays-a-mobility-revolution-led-by-tns-first-women-auto-drivers-union mobility], and [https://www.newindianexpress.com/cities/chennai/2025/Nov/29/a-groundbreaking-film-captures-the-resilience-humour-and-solidarity-of-indias-first-women-auto-drivers-union-redefining-who-belongs-on-the-citys-streets women’s access to public space in urban India].
The film had its world premiere in competition at the International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam (IDFA) 2025. It secured support from the Good Media Network Impact Fund through the Good Media Pitch in Berlin.
Synopsis
Auto Queens centres on Mohana, the president of VPMS, and Leela Rani, a fellow union member, as they navigate Chennai’s streets and negotiate the structural and social challenges of working in a male-dominated transport sector. The film juxtaposes their contrasting personalities with their shared commitment to collective organising, highlighting both the precarity and resilience of women’s labour in informal urban economies.
Production
Auto Queens was produced by Storiculture through the Earthbound/100 Impact Accelerator, supported by Mantra Foundation and Omidyar Network India. Earthbound is a platform curating an ecosystem of 100 transformative media projects.
The film originated in a series of media camps conducted with members of Veera Pengal Munnetra Sangam (VPMS) in Chennai, organised by Earthbound in partnership with Empowering Communities Through Education (ECTE).
Release and Screenings
The film [https://www.outlookindia.com/art-entertainment/movie-review/idfa-2025-auto-queens-review-tamil-doc-spotlights-indias-first-female-auto-driver-collective premiered] in competition at IDFA 2025 and has since been screened at festivals, curated programmes, and impact-oriented forums focused on gender, labour rights, and urban mobility.
A private, closed-door screening of Auto Queens was held in Chennai on 14 December 2025 for the women of VPMS and their families.
Themes
The documentary explores sisterhood, women’s labour, gendered access to public space, and informal transport economies, situating the experiences of women auto-rickshaw drivers within broader conversations on mobility, urban infrastructure and dignity of work in Indian cities.
